plan: In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of the number of bidders or their behavior. This is because you pay the second-highest bid if you win, not your own bid, so there's no incentive to shade your bid. Bidding exactly my value ensures I win whenever profitable (value > second-highest bid) and lose when it wouldn't be profitable. With no prior history in this single-round game, truthful bidding is optimal.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of the number of competitors. Since I pay the second-highest bid if I win, bidding exactly my value ensures I win whenever it's profitable (value > second-highest bid) and never overpay. There's no incentive to shade the bid up or down. I will bid my true value of $31.

This is a second-price (Vickrey) auction with private values. In such auctions, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of what others do—if you bid higher, you risk overpaying; if you bid lower, you risk losing profitable wins. Since this is a one-shot game with no repeated learning needed, I will bid exactly my value of $24 to maximize expected profit.
